title: Finite-degree Noetherian cohomological approximation of a relative complex
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a separated finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ be pseudo-coherent relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-derived-category, def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology and $H^i(E)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$. For each integer $n$, there exist a commutative Noetherian ring $A_0$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], a ring map $A_0\to A$, a separated finite type morphism $f_0:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, a morphism $u:X\to X_0$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, a closed immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A_0}\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product] whose composite with the projection to $X_0$ is $u$, and $E_0\in D(\mathcal O_{X_0})$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], together with a morphism $\gamma:E_0\to Ru_*E$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], such that the adjoint of the induced map on derived global sections is a morphism
$$\alpha:A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_0}R\Gamma(X_0,E_0)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X,E)$$
in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], inducing an isomorphism on $H^i$ for $i>n$ and a surjection on $H^n$. Derived tensor means tensoring a K-flat resolution [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; $R\Gamma$ means derived global sections of the structure-module sheaves. If $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], the data can be chosen with $f_0$ proper. Neither $X$ nor $E$ is required to be the ordinary base change of $X_0$ or $E_0$, and the data may depend on $n$.

source.place: Agent-formulated finite-degree descente input for the unnumbered general assertion following Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; the assertion cites Kiehl, Ein Descente-Lemma und Grothendiecks Projektionssatz fuer nichtnoethersche Schemata (1972). The Stacks paragraph does not state or prove this approximation lemma; primary source WANTED, as recorded in report.md. The quasi-coherence and upper bound are also in more-morphisms.tex, Tag 09UI, definition-relative-pseudo-coherence, following paragraph, and Tag 0CSU, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence.

proof.text: For each integer i use relative (i-1)-pseudo-coherence and the high-cohomology lemma to obtain quasi-coherence of H^i(E). The source X is qcqs, since f is separated finite type over an affine. For upper boundedness use relative 0-pseudo-coherence: on its affine charts U embedded as closed subschemes of affine spaces over base charts, Ri_*(E|U) admits locally a bounded finite free complex mapping to it isomorphically in degrees >0. Such a complex is zero in sufficiently high degrees. The affine ambient chart is quasi-compact, so finitely many such neighborhoods give a bound there. The closed immersion is affine; now that E|U is in D_QCoh, t-exactness and conservativity of affine derived pushforward transfer this bound to E|U. Quasi-compactness of X gives a finite chart subcover and hence a single upper bound on E. The empty source has E=0.

proof.text: The base Spec A is qcqs. Take the constructed finite-presentation envelope Env_fp(X/Spec A); its properties give a closed immersion X into a separated finitely presented Spec A-scheme V. If f is proper, instead use the proper finite-presentation envelope, so that V is proper and finitely presented over Spec A. Keep this chosen closed immersion throughout the construction. In particular this does not assert X=V.

proof.text: Express Spec A as the inverse limit of spectra of finitely generated Z-subalgebras. Finite-presentation spreading out descends V to a finitely presented Y over one such ring B. These finite type Z-schemes are Noetherian, hence qcqs; the separatedness-descent lemma applies and permits increasing the stage so Y/B is separated. Equivalently V=Y_A, so the chosen immersion becomes j:X into Y_A. In the proper case use proper Noetherian-stage descent for the proper finitely presented V to choose Y/B proper, still with V=Y_A. B is Noetherian and Y is Noetherian and qcqs. No descent of X or E is being asserted at this step.

source.place: Agent assembly proof; see the cited node statements and the Kiehl-descente paragraph following Tag 0CSD

proof.text: Choose once and for all N>=1 such that, for every affine h:W to this fixed qcqs Y and every quasi-coherent G on W, H^p(W,G)=0 for p>=N. Fix the requested integer n and put a=n-N+1. Apply prescribed-envelope sheaf descente to B, Y, j, E and a. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1 and 3. Obtain B', Z, F, gamma, theta and C with H^i(C)=0 for i>=a. The map Z to Y is affine: over an affine Spec R in Y, its inverse image is a closed subscheme of Spec(R tensor_B B'), hence is affine by the closed-immersion definition and the affine fibre-product calculation. Thus the SAME N bounds cohomology of every quasi-coherent module on Z, independently of the new coefficient algebra B'. This order of choices avoids a circular cohomology-bound argument.

source.place: Agent assembly proof; see the cited node statements and the Kiehl-descente paragraph following Tag 0CSD

proof.text: On Mod(O_Z), Gamma(Z,-) commutes with countable products, since limits of module sheaves and their sections are formed sectionwise. Apply the unbounded derived-functor bound with F=Gamma, the N of step 4, and b=a-1=n-N to C. The sheaf-descente conclusion gives C in D_QCoh and H^i(C)=0 for i>b. Therefore H^i(RGamma(Z,C))=0 for i>b+N-1=n-1, in particular for every i>=n. Derived global sections take the cone triangle T -> Ru_*E -> C -> T[1] to a distinguished triangle. In its long exact sequence the two adjacent cone groups vanish for i>n, so RGamma(theta) is an isomorphism there; H^n(RGamma C)=0 gives surjectivity in degree n. This argument allows C to be unbounded below.

source.place: Agent assembly proof; see the cited node statements and the Kiehl-descente paragraph following Tag 0CSD

proof.text: Use the canonical projection mate for q:Z -> Spec B', with M=tilde A and L=F. Both schemes and q are qcqs (Z is closed in the finite type B'-scheme Y_B', and B' is Noetherian). M and F have quasi-coherent cohomology. Since q is qcqs, Rq_*F has quasi-coherent cohomology by qcqs direct-image quasi-coherence; the K-injective global-section/direct-image acyclicity lemma, applied to q and a K-injective resolution of F, gives RGamma(Spec B',Rq_*F)=RGamma(Z,F) and likewise RGamma(Spec B',Rq_*T)=RGamma(Z,T). By the affine derived equivalence, Rq_*F is the associated-sheaf complex of N=RGamma(Z,F) and M is that of A. Choose a K-flat resolution P of A over B'; the affine derived tensor chart comparison gives M tensor^L (N)~ = (Tot(P tensor_B' N))~, and the affine equivalence takes its RGamma to A tensor^L_B' N. Consequently this mate identifies RGamma(Z,T) with A tensor^L_B' RGamma(Z,F). The K-injective global-section/direct-image acyclicity comparison identifies RGamma(Z,Ru_*E) with RGamma(X,E), without requiring u flat. Under these identifications RGamma(theta) is the scalar-extension adjoint of RGamma(gamma): indeed the projection mate is by definition the transpose of pullback tensor the counit; theta was defined using that same counit and the A-action. Composing with the scalar-extension unit x -> 1 tensor x gives RGamma(gamma), because 1 acts as the identity. Uniqueness of the adjoint proves the identification of the actual map alpha. All scalar tensors are derived (K-flat), not ordinary tensors. Forgetting from A-modules to B'-modules is exact and detects bijectivity and surjectivity, so the degree conclusions of step 5 apply in D(A).

proof.text: Set A_0=B', X_0=Z, E_0=F, f_0=q, and use j' and u supplied by sheaf descente. The morphism Y_B' -> Spec B' is separated finite type by base change. The closed immersion k:Z -> Y_B' is finite, so its composite q is separated finite type. The same local-lemma conclusion supplies j', its required projection u, bounded coherent cohomology of E_0, and gamma. In the proper case Y/B was chosen proper in step 3; proper base change makes Y_B'/B' proper, and the closed-immersion properness lemma makes q proper. Step 6 supplies precisely the required alpha. The choices were made for the fixed n; none forces ordinary base change of X or E or flatness of A over A_0.

Sources checked: Stacks 0CSU (more-morphisms.tex l.16704), 09UI, 0CSD with the Kiehl paragraph after it, and 08DX(2) (perfect.tex l.403). Steps 1-5 and 7 are correct. Step 1: the 0CSU node with m=i-1 gives quasi-coherence; strictly perfect approximations give the upper bound, carried to E by affine t-exactness, with a finite subcover since X is qcqs. Steps 2-3: the 09ZR envelope (proper version in the proper case), the affine Noetherian approximation, spreading out 01ZM, separatedness descent 01ZQ and the 0A0P proper stage all have their hypotheses met. Step 4: N is chosen on the fixed Y before B'; Z->Y is affine. Step 5: the 08D4 bound with b=a-1, a=n-N+1, gives vanishing for i>n-1, hence an isomorphism above n and a surjection at n. Step 7: base change, finiteness and properness of closed immersions. FIX (C1), step 6: it went from the projection mate to RGamma(Z,T)=A tensor^L_B' RGamma(Z,F) by 'consequently', without citing that Rq_* preserves quasi-coherence, the K-injective acyclicity lemma applied to q, or the tilde/derived-tensor compatibility 08DX(2). The repaired item in fixes/ names all three and adds lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-qcoh and lem-pc-affine-derived-tensor-chart-comparison to uses and proof_deps; no statement changed. New nodes: high-qcoh is exactly 0CSU's first assertion and duplicates no node (rg -L for 0CSU and the label). The prescribed-envelope sheaf-descente node does not restate the item: it fixes the Noetherian Y, works at sheaf level and has no global sections, no cohomological-dimension bound and no envelope; it is plausible via the almost-perfect approximation along A=colim B' over Y x^L_B A, with a WANTED Kiehl source, and E=0, empty X, a non-flat A and large a give no counterexample. Batch-5: proper-closed-in-proper-fp-envelope-part (09ZR) and proper-noetherian-stage (0A0P) are generic limit/Nagata lemmas that reach sec-trace-formula only through the definition def-trf-schematically-dense-open; neither is a step of the trace formula or Poincare duality proofs, so both are accepted. The three declared tool uses are accepted as generic. No SGA citation. Advisory: both new nodes lack lean_audit.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
